summary: End-to-end testing of impaginazione print app. Backend: 11/11 pytest cases pass covering PDF single/duplex (2 pages), PNG/JPG raster, A4 300dpi size (2480x3508), landscape swap, duplex raster ZIP, 400 for image-doesn't-fit, 422 for bad params/invalid sheet, copies limiting. Frontend: full Playwright flow verified - app loads, sheet-dims header updates, image upload (front/back), duplex toggle shows back dropzone + view-front/back buttons, sheet A4/A3 switching, landscape swap, width/height/no-fit-warning for 25x25, lock-ratio-btn correctly scales height (10 -> 6.25 for 800x500 image), layout-info updates (Griglia 2x5 max 10), PNG and PDF downloads trigger with correct filenames (stampa_A4_vert.pdf/png), cut-marks switch toggles, flip-short selectable.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js catch block: `await e.response.data.text()` can throw if e.response is undefined (e.g., network error) - though wrapped in try/catch so acceptable.
layout.js: when p.gap=0 and p.width=0 (invalid), division is guarded by `valid` check - good.
server.py cut_lines uses set rounding at 4 decimals - fine for cm precision.
No file-size limit on upload endpoint; large uploads could DoS. Consider adding max-size validation.
ImageDrop uses global `Image` constructor shadowed implicitly - works because browser `Image` is on window; fine.
seed_data_creation: Generated PNG images in-memory via PIL for both backend pytest and frontend Playwright tests. No persistent data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_generate.py (uses pypdf, PIL). All 11 tests pass in ~3s. Frontend has comprehensive data-testid coverage. No auth, no DB. Only minor concern: no upload size limit on /api/generate.
